Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

L0glm 0.1.0

Initial version

  • A pkgdown documentation website brings together getting-started tutorials, special-family examples, tuning, screening, algorithmic foundations and reproducible benchmarks, with a new hex logo and searchable function reference.

  • L0nnpois() now evaluates held-out deviance and restores validation checkpoints directly in C++. Grouped and independent multichannel fits retain OpenMP, with one shared validation design. Selection and relaxed refitting use the same patience rule, support exclusions and weighted scoring as L0glm.fit(). Candidate timing avoids forced garbage collections.

  • Validation can compare an nsis grid and default or conditional marginal starts, selecting minimum error or a sparse model within one SE of it. Explicit starts retain their zero exclusions. Candidate diagnostics include timings, validation errors and selected batch/start; retained models share one original design matrix. nsis=NULL keeps the GIC-based ISIS batch size.

  • Optional validation-based stopping supports all ordinary GLM families and links, multichannel responses, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox models. Selection and relaxed passes restore their best validation checkpoint, including nuisance parameters. Weighted observations, offsets, coefficient constraints, starting exclusions and SIS/ISIS are supported. Diagnostics report held-out deviance, iteration histories and candidate timings.

  • Stabilized normalized dispersion pilots near interpolation by checking the effective residual dimension. A weak pilot with insufficient residual information is retried once with moderate ridge; probe solves reuse each factorization. Supplied dispersions and fixed-scale families keep their existing behavior. Development workers load the parent’s compiled DLL.

  • Shared backtracking safeguards ordinary GLMs, special families and the native Poisson backend. Smooth updates on fixed support check the current penalized likelihood with dispersion and ridge weights held fixed. Selection cutoffs follow the smooth step; discrete bound-clipping moves retain a finite-mean guard. Trial steps reuse predictors without another ridge solve. Working-model and deviance kernels retain stable distribution-specific arithmetic. Failed backtracking retains the last finite fit with a warning. Feasibility anchors preserve the first-step penalties and eligible terms when the supplied starting predictor is outside the mean domain.

  • Added OpenMP predictor-level threading to SIS/ISIS, controlled by nthreads in sis_glm() or screen.nthreads in L0glm.fit() (default 1). Screening concurrency is independent of BLAS and outcome fitting. Workers use read-only numerical views, private reusable workspaces and private top-candidate heaps; deterministic merging preserves scores, signs, rankings and ties exactly. R errors/interrupts are handled on the main thread, and builds without OpenMP retain a serial fallback. Returned diagnostics report the threads used.

  • Added screen = "auto", "SIS", "ISIS" or "none" to L0glm.fit(). Automatic ISIS activates for at least 10,000 eligible predictors and at least ten times as many predictors as observations. Screened fits default to GIC, relaxed refitting and serial candidate fits, while respecting explicit controls. SIS/ISIS retain original-dimension sparse coefficients, starting-zero exclusions, mandatory terms, and original-p penalty/scoring conventions. nsis and screen.maxit control the outer search; $screening and S3 displays report its history. CV recomputes screening inside each training fold.

  • Shared multichannel selection/refit dispatch and channel/chunk assembly, preserving starting masks, dispersion updates and relaxed-fit behavior.

  • Consolidated the legacy Gaussian path likelihood adapters while preserving their existing weighting, residual-scale and parameter-count conventions.

  • Removed eight unused internal helpers and obsolete commented-out code. Fitting, solver and scoring routines retain their existing implementations.

  • Added S3 predict() and fitted() methods for ordinary/native L0glm models and sparseglm() comparisons, sharing prediction logic with the special families. New-data prediction supports sparse/dense designs, original-scale coefficients, automatic intercepts, named-column matching and explicit offsets. Outputs include GLM/NB means, multinomial probabilities/classes and Cox risks or survival curves. Comparison survival baselines are calculated on demand. Empty new-data matrices are supported; multinomial class ties are deterministic.

  • Added S3 print() and summary() methods for L0glm and native Poisson fits, inherited by special-family fits, and for sparseglm() comparisons. Printing uses stored metadata; summaries compute common fit/recovery scores without refitting. Coefficient previews are bounded while retaining the complete sparse matrix. Convergence displays use the last pass per stage and channel, and comparison summaries retain tuning scores, timings and method-status notes.

  • Added sparseglm() to fit, tune and compare L0glm, ABESS, L0Learn, MCP, SCAD, LASSO, relaxed LASSO and both adaptive LASSO variants. Every candidate uses common likelihood/IC scoring or shared row-fold CV, with training-only adaptive ridge pilots. Results retain sparse original-dimension coefficients, paths, fold diagnostics, timings and explicit failure/availability statuses. L0glm.metrics() is now an S3 generic with a comparison-table method. Native grouped Gaussian, joint multinomial and Cox adapters are included; matrix channel weights are preserved using independent paths where needed. Identity-Poisson WLS approximations require an explicit opt-in. Retired the old benchmark drivers and fit.GLM entry points without compatibility wrappers, and migrated their examples to the new interface.

  • Fits now inherit from L0glm_fit, providing coef(), logLik(), nobs(), standard AIC()/BIC() and S3 GIC()/EBIC()/MBIC() extraction for ordinary, native Poisson and special-family models. Original prior weights, offsets and dispersion-estimation flags are retained for correct on-demand scoring. L0glm.metrics() now also supports ordinary models and optional beta_true recovery scores. The help pages explain likelihood conventions, parameter counts, conditional within-row scores and removed diagnostics.

  • Recovery metrics now report channel-entry confusion counts, precision, recall, F1 and MCC within correctly recovered nonmandatory rows of multichannel fits. The pooled scores are conditional on recovering the row; row-support metrics still account for missed and spurious rows. Coefficient summaries retain MAE, RMSE and through-origin R-squared. Selected-coefficient summaries, signed mean error, sMAPE, regression slope, support-size ratio, accuracy and specificity were removed. Historical result tables are preserved; retired diagnostics in benchmark scripts were removed and the solver benchmark now includes MCC/RMSE.

  • Normalized dense Gaussian identity fits reuse fixed weighted cross-products for LLT/LDLT solves with at most 2,000 coefficients. The cache follows the shrinking active set; effectively wide and sparse systems retain their existing solver paths. Adaptive penalties and dispersion updates are unchanged.

  • Normalized dense fits avoid repeated prediction-column copies when most coefficients remain active. Restricted-domain links retain their previous summation order, preserving the difficult Gamma square-root-link fit.

  • Eigen CG now defaults to inner relative tolerance 1e-10, improving agreement with LLT in the Gaussian PSF benchmark. Explicit solver tolerances are retained; LSCG keeps its default 1e-7. This does not change LLT or the outer tolerance.

  • Restored the fitting defaults maxit = 25, tol = 1e-10. Increase maxit explicitly for problems requiring more iterations; returned convergence diagnostics distinguish stopping at the iteration limit from convergence. Single-channel native fits no longer detect unused OpenMP core counts. Dispersion pilots use sparse row augmentation for large dense-stored designs containing mostly exact zeros, preserving the same ridge system and main solver storage.

  • Numeric scalar start = 1 now denotes ones in normalized coefficient coordinates, including a free centered intercept. All other scalars and explicit vectors/matrices retain original input units. This applies to both fitters, multichannel fits, and independently initialized tuning/CV fits.

  • Added normalize = "auto" (default), "none", "l2", "rms", and "sd". RMS gives L2 norm sqrt(n). Automatic initialization, numerical thresholds and convergence use compatible coordinates, while coefficients, explicit vector/matrix starts and ridge targets retain the original input units. Centering requires an unrestricted intercept: nonnegative intercepts remain constrained, and binomial/quasibinomial intercepts retain their exception.

  • Wide Eigen and native Poisson systems use typed Woodbury solves, including unpenalized nuisance terms. Dense CG uses diagonal preconditioning; sparse CG keeps incomplete Cholesky. Dense/sparse design storage is preserved.

  • Exact zero starts exclude coefficients separately in each channel and screen all-zero rows before fitting. Mandatory terms remain eligible with zero starts. Coefficients are returned as sparse matrices in the original dimensions. Signed multichannel starts pool absolute magnitudes without cancellation.

  • Intercepts and always.include terms are unpenalized. GIC uses the original selectable predictor count before starting-mask or pilot support restriction.

  • Estimated dispersion resumes updating after a support change. A virtually interpolating automatic pilot gets one retry with a moderate ridge penalty. Early stopping and per-channel/per-pass convergence diagnostics are returned.

  • L0glm.tune() accepts a common numeric start or start = "pilot". Independent pilot fits supply a shared seed; each requested lambda is fitted independently from it. Returned starts and fit_args allow direct replay. CV builds pilot seeds and preprocessing separately within each training fold.

  • Removed the slow NNLS ridge solver and its package dependency. Use Eigen, bigGlm, or OSQP. Also removed the unused internal block-fitting helper.

  • Both fitters accept scalar starts for every coefficient and response channel, including an added intercept. Numeric scalar one uses normalized coordinates; other scalar starts repeat in original input units.

  • CV tuning returns the full-data fit_1se alongside fit_best, retaining both from the existing path without any additional fits.

  • The full tuning range starts at lambda_min = 2 by default; a smaller positive bound can be supplied explicitly. Zooming moves each endpoint toward the reference on the log scale. Grids retain unique endpoints and, when there are at least three points, the reference.

  • CV tuning returns lambda_1se, the largest evaluated lambda with mean deviance within one SE of the minimum (using the SE at that minimum). Both panels mark it in blue alongside lambda_best and lambda_preset. Criterion tuning returns NULL for this field; fit_best is unchanged.

  • Tuning plots now use log10(lambda) with a reversed axis in both panels, colored coefficient paths and a mathematical beta-hat label. Top axes show support sizes (row support for multichannel responses) at 16 equally spaced log-scale positions, using the nearest fitted models without adding any fits.

  • Renamed L0glm.tune(IC = ...) to L0glm.tune(tune = ...); the returned selection method is also named tune. Package and benchmark calls are updated.

  • Added tune = "cv", nfolds = 5, and optional foldid assignments. CV holds out rows jointly across channels, initializes every training fit independently, and scores weighted held-out deviance. Training penalties are scaled by their fraction of total prior weight to retain the full-data lambda scale. The plot shows mean deviance +/- one SE, the minimum and the GIC reference preset. Fold scores, assignments and training penalties are returned in cv.

  • L0glm.tune() now initializes every lambda independently. A preset fit no longer excludes features from all other fits. The upper endpoint is checked by fitting it, expanded if necessary, then refined between verified nonzero and zero fits to within 5%; it is not a global-optimality bound. The fitted path coefficients, numerical endpoint and best model are returned.

  • Automatic dispersion initialization is independent of the fitted lambda, using the GIC reference penalty for its permissive scale. This prevents a large lambda from cancelling itself through an inversely scaled dispersion.

  • Tuning scores now include observation weights, offsets and known dispersion. Gaussian scales are profiled per channel when unknown. Corrected the extra scale charge in log likelihood and kept the predictor count separate from estimated scale parameters. Tuning uses a scoring-only prediction floor mu_floor = 1e-8 so that sparse multichannel Poisson fits with zero predictions can be compared. mu_floor = 0 requests exact likelihoods and can give infinite criteria; non-finite values are identified in the plot.

  • L0glm.fit(dispersion = NULL) now uses a permissive weak-ridge pilot and bounded Pearson dispersion updates in the existing IRLS loop. The updates require adequate residual degrees of freedom and freeze after three changes below 1% on unchanged support. No nested fitting is required.

  • Positive dispersion values remain fixed; negative values initialize at their absolute value and are subsequently estimated. Channel-specific mixtures are supported through grouped and parallel fits. Relaxed refits report a fresh residual scale for estimated channels. Poisson, binomial and known-theta negative-binomial dispersion is fixed at 1 on the general path too.

  • Fixed Gaussian coefficient initialization with zero observation weights and its weighted rescaling; the automatic scale pilot preserves the caller’s RNG.

  • L0glm.fit(openmp = TRUE) now dispatches nonnegative identity-link Poisson fits using Eigen Cholesky LLT (method = 1L) to L0nnpois. Use openmp = FALSE to select the general R fitting path. Incompatible solver controls also retain the R path. parallelize and ncores control outcome-level concurrency in the compiled backend. Local Windows PSOCK workers use a clean R session and IPv4 loopback for their master connection.

  • The default L0nnpois penalty is now lambda = "gic".

  • Added the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC, or Pearson’s phi) for support recovery to fit metrics and the README benchmark. Constant support vectors give NA, because their correlation is undefined.

  • Fixed logical configuration flags in the README benchmark and added mirrored signal panels, full coefficient scatter plots, and support panels with dark blue true positives, red false positives and magenta false negatives.

  • Audited package and benchmark solver calls and migrated remaining historical Eigen method numbers, including Cholesky LLT from 7L to 1L.

  • Information-criterion names are now consistently case-insensitive in both fitters, tuning and benchmark helpers.

  • Added a shared information-criteria help topic with penalty formulas, usage guidance, original references and the GIC/SIC/HBIC relationship.

  • Fixed metric calculation when true coefficients are not supplied, allowing information-criterion tuning on observed data without simulation truth.

  • Removed lower and upper from L0glm.fit() and L0nnpois(). General box constraints are no longer part of either fitting interface.

  • L0glm.fit(nonnegative = TRUE) constrains all coefficients, including any intercept and always.include terms. Binomial and quasibinomial intercepts remain unrestricted; columns of ones supplied in X are recognized too. The default nonnegative = FALSE allows coefficients of either sign.

  • Removed nonnegative from L0nnpois(): its coefficients, including any intercept, are now always nonnegative. Remove this argument from existing calls, and use L0glm.fit(nonnegative = FALSE) for unrestricted fits.

  • Applied the same constraint rules to initialization, grouped and relaxed fits, and serial and parallel execution. The NNLS ridge backend now handles unrestricted coefficients, including the binomial intercept.

  • Updated help, examples and benchmarks to use the simplified interfaces.
